# Bounded self-cleaning live-Jira-Cloud coordinator lifecycle lane + search-index-lag hardening

## Problem
The epic's Live-External AC requires the RP-03 create-coordinator's create / binding-lifecycle /
commit-unknown / fuse exercised against **live Jira Cloud**. The only Cloud lane today is read-only AND
gated off (`vars.AWS_S3_REHEARSAL_ROLE_ARN` unset) — SKIPPED even in green runs — so **no run has exercised
live-Cloud mutation**. Separately, `bridge check-access`'s `STEP_JQL_SEARCH` flakes on live REB: its wait
is a FIXED 6x5s (no backoff), shorter than Jira Cloud's Lucene-index eventual-consistency lag — the write
lands (the by-key read right after passes), only SEARCH visibility lags.

## §1 — Harden the search-index wait (`access_check.py`)
Replace the fixed 6x5s loop with an env-tunable exponential-backoff budget:
- `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_RETRIES` (default 10; was 6), `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP` base secs (default 3; was 5),
  `JIRA_PROBE_JQL_SLEEP_MAX` cap secs (default 30).
- Sleep before retry k (k over 0..RETRIES-2) is `min(base*2**k, cap)` → defaults `[3,6,12,24,30,30,30,30,30]`
  = 195s worst case, covering the observed lag (old ~25s budget timed out) with margin. Reuses the
  ADR-0036 capped-exponential SHAPE (`_errors.MAX_BACKOFF_S` style) already used by the acli retry floor,
  but as a positive-result visibility poll (not a transient-error retry). The `sleep_fn` injectable seam is
  kept so the schedule is unit-testable without real sleeping, and this poll helper is reused by §2's
  commit-unknown visibility wait.

## §2 — Live-Cloud coordinator lifecycle module (bounded, self-cleaning)
NEW `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_mutation/test_cloud_coordinator_lifecycle.py` (+ `conftest.py`). Against
live REB it drives the epic's CREATE route `rebar_reconciler.create_route.coordinate_full_create`
(create_route.py:171) — composing `coordinate_create` (create_coordinator.py:235; create+commit-unknown)
with `contain_created` (label/property/confirm binding) — for a plan of EXACTLY ONE throwaway ticket, then
folds the outcome through the fuse:
- **Write-bounding (shared-prod safety).** No full `bridge sync`; no legacy-route `--filter-local-ids`
  (request.py:95 rejects it here). It acts only on the ONE plan handed to it (one
  create per plan), so there is NO enumeration and NO inbound write-back — the only Jira mutations possible
  are the throwaway issue's create, its containment label/property, and its delete.
- **create + binding-lifecycle.** `create_execute` issues the physical create via the live Cloud client and
  returns the key; `record_key`/`attach_label`/`set_property`/`confirm` bind+contain it; the module asserts
  a confirmed containment (`dependents_released`) with `jira` channel + `jira-` local-id provenance.
- **commit-unknown recovery.** A second call injects an AMBIGUOUS create signal (simulated timeout) so
  `_resolve_ambiguous` (create_coordinator.py:211) re-observes EXACTLY ONCE and ADOPTS the existing issue
  (recovered) instead of duplicating. Its `observe` FIRST waits until the dedup label search reflects the
  created issue (reusing §1's helper), so adoption is attributable to the dedup path and cannot flake on lag.
- **fuse.** The create outcome is folded through `PassFuse` (pass_fuse.py) via
  `batch_dispatch.coordinate_and_fuse` over the throwaway outcome; the module asserts the returned
  `CutoverReport` carries the fuse tally/decisions for the throwaway identity.
- **teardown (always) + one label scheme.** ONE env label `${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}` (workflow: `rebar-id:cloudprobe-<github.run_id>`; local:
  `rebar-id:cloudprobe-<uuid>`) is STAMPED on the created issue by `attach_label`. The module deletes the
  issue by key in a `finally` (mirrors access_check.py:217-224), then sweeps any issue carrying THAT SAME
  label — the identical value §3's sweep keys on, so the two cannot diverge; scoped to this run only, never
  the shared `rebar-id:` prefix.
- Gated by module-level `_live_jira_ready()` + `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1` + Cloud creds, enrolling in the
  all-skip canary (`tests/external/conftest.py`) like the DC modules.

## §3 — Workflow lane
Add `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` to `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` +
weekly cron): export `REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL=rebar-id:cloudprobe-${{ github.run_id }}` + REB Cloud env from
secrets, run `bridge check-access` (preflight) THEN the new module, and on BOTH failure AND cancel run an
always-run teardown sweeping `${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}` via acli — `acli jira workitem search --jql
"labels = ..." --json` then `acli jira workitem delete --key <KEY> --yes` per hit (`--yes` REQUIRED per the
acli.py bug-3256 note so the non-TTY sweep does not block on stdin and leak). Same label the module stamps,
scoping the sweep to the current run only.

## §4 — Workflow-structure unit test
`tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py` (modelled on
`test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`) proves the lane exists, exports `REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL` from the
run id, runs check-access + the module, and has an always-run teardown with `--yes` keyed on that label.

## §5 — Docs
Update `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/README.md`: the read-only cardinal rule is that suite's own
design choice; the new mutating lane is bounded, self-cleaning, and shared-prod-safe.

## Consumers to update (enumerated)
- `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` currently asserts `search_issues.call_count == 6`
  and `delays == [5,5,5,5,5]`. Updated in the SAME change to assert the new default 10 attempts and backoff
  `delays == [3,6,12,24,30,30,30,30,30]` (computed from the same constants/env defaults, not magic
  numbers), plus an env-override case recomputing the schedule from an overridden base/cap/retries.

## Surface-parity census
- CLI (`bridge check-access`): in scope — JQL backoff exercised through it.
- library (`run_access_check`; `coordinate_full_create`+`PassFuse`): in scope — unit tests drive the backoff; the live module drives the create route + fuse.
- automated caller (lane / live module): in scope — E2E oracle is the live run.
- MCP/API: out of scope — none is an MCP tool.
- dual-direction: only the outbound create exists in a one-plan call, so no mirror direction to cover.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `access_check.py` JQL wait is env-tunable exponential backoff (defaults 10 / 3 / 30 → sleeps
  `[3,6,12,24,30,...]`); `sleep_fn` seam preserved; write-landing still confirmed by the by-key read.
  Evidenced by new unit tests asserting the schedule and env-override recomputation.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py` updated to the new schedule/defaults and passes.
- [ ] The live-Cloud module drives `coordinate_full_create` for ONE throwaway plan (create/binding +
  commit-unknown-after-visibility-wait + fuse), asserts known_key is the throwaway key and no other, and
  ALWAYS deletes (finally + `${REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL}` sweep). Enrols in the all-skip canary. Evidenced by
  the module passing in a dispatched live run.
- [ ] The `jira-cloud-mutation-probe` lane exports `REBAR_PROBE_RUN_LABEL`, runs check-access + the module,
  and has an always-run `acli ... delete --key <KEY> --yes` teardown keyed on that label. Evidenced by §4.
- [ ] A dispatched Live External Integration run shows the new Cloud-mutation lane GREEN and the DC lane
  GREEN. Evidenced by the run URL commented on the epic.
- [ ] `make lint && make typecheck && make test` green.

## Verify commands
- `make test PYTEST_ARGS="tests/scripts/bridge/test_jira_capability_probe.py tests/unit/test_external_integration_cloud_mutation_workflow.py"` and `make lint`

## Portability
CI-agnostic: the backoff is library behavior (no CI trigger); the new lane surfaces an operation-linked
probe (`rebar bridge check-access` + a pytest module driving `coordinate_full_create`) that also runs
locally with the same env — no capability is gated solely on a specific CI system.
